title: Disabled peer delivers first AI-cloned parliamentary speech
source_used: AFP, read on its copy at The Economic Times (the Times page was blocked; Tech Xplore and ITV pages were blocked); Vietnam.vn relay checked for the committee approval
key_facts: On Tuesday 13 Oct 2026, Baroness Jane Campbell of Surbiton, a peer in the House of Lords, became the first person to use an AI-generated voice to deliver a speech in the UK parliament (AFP).
She is 67, an independent crossbench peer, and struggles to speak naturally because of spinal muscular atrophy, a condition that worsens over time.
AI software recreated her voice as it used to be and read a speech she wrote herself, during a health debate.

The Lords procedure committee, which considers protocol, gave her permission; in 2012 it had allowed her to have a personal assistant read her speeches, departing from a 1707 ruling that bars non-peers from the floor.

Campbell approached ElevenLabs, a company that specialises in natural-sounding speech, to recreate her voice; its Gabi Leibowitz told AFP the voice was fine-tuned with her to sound authentic to her voice before illness.
ElevenLabs says 30 seconds of audio can be enough to clone a voice, though 30 minutes to an hour is recommended for best quality.
She told the chamber it showed 'inclusion in democracy at its best' and introduced 'Baroness Campbell Mark 2'.
A Vietnam.vn relay of the Lords announcement (12 Oct) says the committee had approved the use and that the Lord Speaker, Lord Forsyth of Drumlean, welcomed it.
quote_evidence: A British lawmaker made history on Tuesday by becoming the first person to use an AI-generated voice to deliver a speech in the UK parliament.
During a debate about health on Tuesday, AI software was used to recreate the sound of her voice, as it used to be, to read a speech she wrote herself.
Campbell received permission from the procedure committee -- which considers protocol in the Lords, whose origins date back to the 11th century -- to use the technology.
why_it_matters_hint: A peer who is losing her voice delivered a speech in a recreated version of it, with the Lords' formal permission, a first for the UK parliament.
notes: The Times page returned no text; the story was read from AFP's report as carried by The Economic Times, and the Lords approval is also given by a Vietnam.vn relay of 12 Oct and the Lords press office as quoted by AFP. Tech Xplore and ITV pages were blocked.
